findings.title: Copyright holder identified by GitHub handle 'AIwork4me' rather than a legal name
findings.detail: The notice 'Copyright (c) 2026 AIwork4me' names an account handle. This is permissible (a copyright notice may identify the holder by any stable designation) and matches the user's own authorization wording, which uses 'AIwork4me' as the owning party; no documentation claims legal-entity status. Informational only: upstream maintainers may at review time ask for the holder's real name; changing it later would be another COPYRIGHT_TEXT-only delta requiring the same re-hash/re-validation steps already documented for DCO rewording.
findings.evidence: All four new files, line 5; COPYRIGHT_AND_DCO_STATUS.md §2 quote of the authorization.
findings.recommendation: No action required; confirm at submission time that the user is comfortable with the handle as the public notice.

findings.title: Sign-off email uses the legacy bare-username noreply form; evidence chain unaffected
findings.detail: AIwork4me@users.noreply.github.com is the legacy noreply format (accounts created after 2017 default to id+username@, i.e. 261514469+AIwork4me@users.noreply.github.com). The Phase 5 record does not depend on the format: it rests on the observed API linkage (author.login=AIwork4me) for both the pushed commit 7294c66 (this email) and the web-UI merge 033e6f4 (qq.com email), which is sound. The recorded sign-off instructions use the same email for author and sign-off, so any DCO-bot author-email==signoff-email check would pass. Purely informational for the human at submission time (they may prefer the id+ form or AIwork4me@qq.com, both already recorded as legitimate).

checks.question: Are the copyright assertions authorized and scoped to exactly the four series-created files, with no over-claiming?
checks.evidence: The four files carrying 'Copyright (c) 2026 AIwork4me' are all created by this series: miopen_freestanding_type_traits.hpp + miopen_freestanding_utility.hpp added by d4003de1 (commit 1), miopen_freestanding_initializer_list.hpp added by 3b18a065 (commit 2), test/hiprtc_selfcontained.cpp added by e7ff6d75 (commit 3) — verified via git diff-tree --diff-filter=A per commit. git diff base..HEAD greps for copyright lines show ONLY four '+' lines, all inside those new files; zero copyright lines removed or altered anywhere. Modified pre-existing files (miopen_type_traits.hpp, miopen_utility.hpp, radix.hpp, tensor_view.hpp, both CMakeLists.txt) retain their 'Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.' notices unchanged — no AMD code claimed. P5→P5.1 delta verified independently: git diff 29846fc4..e7ff6d75 = 4 files, +4/−4, each hunk exactly '[contributor name and notice to be set by the submitter]' → 'AIwork4me', MIT license text otherwise byte-identical. Code-level inspection of all four new files found no third-party markers (no AMD/LLVM/libc++ notices, no _LIBCPP internals); the trait/forward/initializer_list definitions are minimal implementations of interfaces and layouts mandated by the C++ standard and clang's lowering, so the documentation's 'no third-party code' statement is defensible. Documentation does not claim legal-entity status or copyright over anything not authored here.
